title: Trust, but Verify: Shreya Rajpal
talk_summary: Shreya Rajpal (Guardrails AI) argues that because LLM outputs are non-deterministic, you should wrap every model call in a verification suite that checks outputs against constraints and, on violation, re-asks the model with the specific violation injected. She stresses grounding checks in external systems, cheap deterministic validators/classifiers instead of LLMs, and only returning output once verification passes.

takeaways.technique: Constraint-checker + regenerate loop on LLM output
takeaways.what_they_do: Every LLM output passes a verification suite; on failure they inject the violated rule and the bad output back into a re-ask prompt so the model self-corrects, then re-verify.

takeaways.technique: Ground checks in an external executable system
takeaways.what_they_do: For code/SQL generation they hook LLM output into a runtime sandbox containing real schema/data and re-ask until it actually runs, rather than trusting the model's claim.
takeaways.evidence_quote: hook up the output of the llm into a runtime that basically contains application specific data
takeaways.numbers: claims 'substantially improve the correctness' of SQL queries (no number)

takeaways.technique: Cheap deterministic validators instead of LLM checks
takeaways.what_they_do: Use rule-based heuristics and small high-precision classifiers for basic constraints rather than spending an LLM call on them.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you don't need like a jackhammer to crack open a walnut

takeaways.what_they_do: Ran the same eval five times at zero temperature and got different numbers, showing LLM evaluators are not stable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we ran the exact same experiment five different times changing like absolutely zero parameters with zero temperature and saw like different numbers
takeaways.numbers: 5 identical runs, zero temperature, differing benchmark numbers

takeaways.what_they_do: On a failed check they choose a policy: re-ask, filter, programmatic fix, fall back to another system, or refuse/noop with logging, rather than a single retry behavior.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you have a set of these policies including like reasing ... filtering or fixing ... falling back on some other system ... refraining from answering

takeaways.technique: Compile verification rules into the prompt
takeaways.what_they_do: Their spec language compiles the chosen validators into the prompt so the model is told the requirements up front, not just checked after.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a specification language that allows you to compile your requirements into a prom prompt
